title: OES-32 toy simulation (quantum-error-correction-demo)
description:
Classical Python toy simulation of OES-32-style metrics. No qubits, no QEC code; every output is SYNTHETIC. A single classical Python script runs a Monte Carlo loop over hand-written formulas relating a simulated erasure probability to "coherence", "success rate", and a few other labelled quantities; it is a teaching/exploration toy for the OES-32 naming used across the Spark AI NLP repositories.

Evidence tags. Every printed metric: SYNTHETIC (formula output on generated inputs). The success rate (for example, 94.92%) is SYNTHETIC: recovery success is drawn with probability max(0.95, 1 − 0.7·p_erasure), so it is ≈95% by construction and is not a measured error-correction rate. Any hardware, qubit, or QEC performance interpretation: not claimed.

Relationship to ADR-001. The normative OES-32 residual is oes32-residual@b77b612; this demo is not bit-matched to it and is not a Profile A sidecar.

Scope and limits. Not a quantum computer implementation and not a quantum error-correcting code (no qubits, no stabilizers, no surface code, no decoder); not a benchmark (metric names such as "spooky correlation" and "entanglement entropy" are labels for formulas, not quantum measurements); not hardware, field, medical, or production software. The repository name predates these scope statements and is kept so existing links keep working.

Evidence tags follow sparkainlp-x/.github (SYNTHETIC / REPORTED / TARGET / UNRUN).
